title: Traumatic brain injury and concussion in the hospital
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM code for the head injury (only that code).
note:
Admission Date: 05/12/2026
Discharge Date: 05/18/2026
Reason for Admission: Fall from a ladder with head trauma.

Vitals:
BP: 138/84 mmHg
HR: 78 bpm
RR: 16 breaths/min
Temp: 98.6 F
SpO2: 97% on room air

Recent Labs:
WBC: 8.4 x 10^9/L
Hemoglobin: 12.4 g/dL
Platelets: 210 x 10^9/L
eGFR: 62 mL/min/1.73m2
Sodium: 139 mEq/L
Potassium: 4.1 mEq/L

Review of Systems:
The patient reports mild headaches and some fatigue. She denies any dizziness, visual disturbances, or difficulty with balance. She denies any nausea or vomiting.

Social History:
The patient is retired and lives at home with her daughter. She does not smoke and does not use any recreational substances.

Family History:
Mother had hypertension. Father had a history of heart disease.

Hospital Course:
The patient is a 79-year-old woman who presented to the emergency department following a fall from a ladder. She reported that she did not lose consciousness at any time during the event. Initial evaluation was significant for mild disorientation. Imaging revealed a diffuse brain injury on the MRI. The patient was admitted for observation and management of neurological symptoms. Over the course of her stay, she showed steady improvement in cognitive clarity and physical mobility. She was able to participate in physical therapy and successfully completed a bedside mobility assessment. She tolerated her diet well and remained stable throughout her admission. She is now cleared for discharge to home with supportive care.

Discharge Diagnoses:
- Diffuse brain injury
- Fall from ladder

Discharge Medications:
- Acetaminophen 650mg every 6 hours as needed for pain.
- Multivitamin daily.

Follow-up:
The patient will follow up with her primary care physician in one week for a routine neurological check. She was instructed to seek immediate medical attention if she experiences worsening headaches or confusion.

Electronically signed,
D. Kowalski, MD
05/18/2026
explanations: Diffuse traumatic brain injury without loss of consciousness, initial encounter: S06.2X0A (HCC 399).

distractors.why: No loss of consciousness is documented.

hccs.label: Major Head Injury without Loss of Consciousness
